raw_case_text:
A 23-month-old girl presented to our facility with one week of worsening fevers, productive cough, and increased work of breathing. Over the previous 3 months, she was treated for presumed upper respiratory tract infections with inhaled beta-agonists, inhaled steroids, oral steroids, and several different oral antibiotics. Relevant medical history was significant for prematurity and severe anemia necessitating intrauterine blood transfusions, CDA diagnosed at 20 months by bone marrow biopsy and aspiration that was morphologically consistent with type II, and surgical placement of a Port-a-Cath for chronic blood transfusions.
Initial vital signs were temperature 37.9 degrees Celsius, heart rate 156 bpm, respiratory rate 50/min with oxygen saturation 83% on room air and 98% on 1 LPM oxygen by nasal cannula, and blood pressure 115/61 mm Hg. She appeared in mild distress with increased work of breathing. She had moderate frontal bossing with open anterior fontanelle. Heart examination was significant for a II/IV systolic ejection murmur. Lung exam revealed diffuse rales bilaterally but no wheezing. Abdomen was not distended. The liver was palpated 4 cm below the costal margin, and the spleen palpated to the level of the umbilicus. She had no clubbing, cyanosis, or peripheral edema.
Chest radiograph showed diffuse ground glass alveolar infiltrates which were chronic in nature when compared to a chest X-ray from one year prior (Figure 1). Blood, urine, and respiratory cultures were sent, and the patient was started empirically on oral azithromycin and parenteral ceftriaxone.
On day 3, a transthoracic echocardiogram revealed a patent foramen ovale but no cardiomyopathic process. An abdominal ultrasound confirmed hepatosplenomegaly. Repeat chest X-ray showed no changes, and chest CT was offered but the parents refused.
Despite 4 days of antibiotics, the patient continued to spike intermittent fevers and was still on oxygen treatment, and there still were no changes on chest radiograph. Bronchoscopy was performed and was anatomically normal. The bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) fluid was cloudy in appearance and revealed no evidence of aspiration or malignant cells. Grocott's methenamine silver (GMS) stain was negative for Pneumocystis jirovecii. Ziehl-Neelsen stain was negative for acid-fast bacilli (AFB). Fungal, bacterial, AFB, RSV, and influenza cultures of BAL fluid revealed no growth. Differential of the WBCs indicated 68% macrophages, 12% PMNs, and 10% lymphocytes. Light microscopic examination of BAL fluid using Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) stain was positive for abundant amorphous material within the pulmonary macrophages and also in larger extracellular aggregates suggesting pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (Figure 2). The lipid-laden macrophage (LLM) index was 120.
On day 5, the patient's work of breathing improved, lung sounds improved, and the supplemental oxygen was decreased to 0.5 LPM by nasal cannula. Antibacterials were discontinued. On day 7, BAL fluid was positive for cytomegalovirus (CMV) by indirect fluorescent antibody testing and serum CMV IgG and IgM antibodies were detected by immunoassay, while CMV DNA of the blood remained negative. Ophthalmologic examination revealed no signs of CMV retinitis. The patient was started on parenteral ganciclovir. On day 9, the patient was weaned off supplemental oxygen to room air. She continued IV ganciclovir and was discharged from the hospital.
After completion of two weeks of ganciclovir, the patient presented to her hematologist's office for scheduled followup and blood transfusion. Chest X-ray was repeated and showed minimal interval improvement in the diffuse coarse reticular opacities noted on X-ray from her most recent hospitalization. Again, the parents refused CT scan. The patient was subsequently lost to followup. Several months later she was admitted to a hospital in another state in respiratory failure. Per report, she required intubation and BAL was performed, which confirmed PAP.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 23-month-old girl with type II congenital dyserythropoietic anemia presented with a 1-week history of worsening fevers, productive cough, and increased work of breathing.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed 1 week of escalating fevers, productive cough, and respiratory distress. Over the preceding 3 months, she had been repeatedly treated for presumed upper respiratory tract infections with inhaled beta-agonists, inhaled corticosteroids, oral corticosteroids, and multiple courses of oral antibiotics without resolution.
subjective.past_medical_history: Prematurity with severe fetal anemia requiring intrauterine blood transfusions; congenital dyserythropoietic anemia (CDA) type II diagnosed at 20 months of age by bone marrow aspirate and biopsy; surgical placement of an indwelling Port-a-Cath for chronic blood transfusions.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for worsening fevers, productive cough, and increased work of breathing; negative for cyanosis, clubbing, or peripheral edema.

objective.physical_examination: Initial vital signs: Temperature 37.9 °C, heart rate 156 beats/min, respiratory rate 50 breaths/min, blood pressure 115/61 mmHg, and SpO2 83% on room air (improving to 98% on 1 L/min nasal cannula oxygen). General and systemic exam: Mild respiratory distress with increased work of breathing; moderate frontal bossing with an open anterior fontanelle; grade II/IV systolic ejection murmur; diffuse bilateral rales without wheezing on lung auscultation; non-distended abdomen with hepatosplenomegaly (liver palpated 4 cm below the costal margin and spleen palpable to the level of the umbilicus); no clubbing, cyanosis, or peripheral edema. Ophthalmologic exam (day 7): No signs of CMV retinitis.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission chest radiograph: Diffuse ground-glass alveolar infiltrates that were chronic when compared against a chest X-ray from 1 year earlier (minimal interval improvement on follow-up CXR 2 weeks post-discharge). Transthoracic echocardiogram (day 3): Patent foramen ovale without cardiomyopathy. Abdominal ultrasound (day 3): Confirmed hepatosplenomegaly. Routine blood, urine, and respiratory cultures: Negative. Virological serology and PCR (day 7): Serum CMV IgG and IgM antibodies positive by immunoassay; peripheral blood CMV DNA PCR negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Bronchoscopy and bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL, day 4): Anatomically normal airways; cloudy BAL fluid with cell differential showing 68% macrophages, 12% PMNs, and 10% lymphocytes, and a lipid-laden macrophage (LLM) index of 120; negative for malignant cells; Grocott's methenamine silver (GMS) stain negative for Pneumocystis jirovecii; Ziehl-Neelsen stain negative for acid-fast bacilli; BAL bacterial, fungal, AFB, RSV, and influenza cultures negative; Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) stain was strongly positive for abundant intracellular and extracellular amorphous proteinaceous material diagnostic of pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP); BAL indirect fluorescent antibody testing (returned day 7) was positive for cytomegalovirus (CMV). Parents declined chest CT.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Secondary pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP; confirmed by abundant PAS-positive amorphous material within pulmonary macrophages and extracellular aggregates on BAL fluid, and re-confirmed on repeat BAL during a subsequent out-of-state admission) with concurrent cytomegalovirus (CMV) pneumonitis (confirmed by BAL indirect fluorescent antibody and positive serum CMV IgM/IgG) in a 23-month-old girl with congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type II; Pneumocystis jirovecii was excluded by negative BAL GMS staining. Plan and clinical course: Empiric oral azithromycin and parenteral ceftriaxone were discontinued on hospital day 5 as work of breathing improved. Following day 7 BAL CMV confirmation, she completed a 2-week course of parenteral ganciclovir, weaned to room air on day 9, and was discharged; several months later, she was hospitalized in another state with acute respiratory failure requiring intubation, where repeat BAL re-confirmed PAP.
